issues.description: Re-ingesting after input files or rows are removed leaves stale results and aliases in the database.
Format B crashes when metrics is present but not an object instead of emitting a malformed_row warning.
Format A accepts non-finite scores such as nan/inf, causing DB integrity crashes or invalid clamped data.
Format B accepts JSON NaN/Infinity scores and can crash during SQLite insertion.
Format C accepts non-finite float score text instead of treating it as missing or malformed.
Malformed XML raises ElementTree.ParseError and aborts the whole ingest.
Duplicate corrections are counted and applied for every source even though the documented correction semantics are Format B-specific.
An empty input directory returns an error but still creates and initializes the SQLite database.
All parsers load complete input files or XML trees into memory, which is risky for large harness outputs.
Test tooling is configured but pytest is not declared in project optional dependencies or a dev extra.
